title: Leave none of the invoice export's lookup threads behind

blocks.text: On the first of every month the billing service exports invoices. The export adds up the tax of a batch of invoices with a parallel stream, and each lookup is an HTTP call to the tax service that can take seconds. Ops noticed that a service which runs exports all day has a thread count that only goes up.

`InvoiceExport` already sums the tax. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/InvoiceExport.java`: `onLookupThreads(...)` runs the lookups in a `ForkJoinPool` of `lookupThreads` threads and returns their result.
When you're done, nothing of the export is left running once `totalTax` returns, also when a lookup throws; that exception reaches the caller. About four lines in total.

cases.says: the export returns the sum of the tax of every invoice
the pool the lookups ran in is shut down by the time the export returns
when a lookup throws, the export throws that exception and its pool is still shut down

origin.section: A Pool You Create Keeps Its Threads Until You Close It

concepts: A pool you create keeps its workers after its last task until you close or shut it down, also when the work throws; idle workers end only slowly.
